time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t*24); frame 0 = t 0

camera.evidence: phase correlation of frame 35 and 71 vs frame 0: shift < 0.003 px
camera.notes: Low camera looking slightly up at a fantasy mushroom meadow; treated as a 2D scene (motion plane facing camera). The butterfly keeps an almost constant image height (body y ~652-660 px) and similar apparent size, so a single px scale is appropriate.

moving_objects.name: butterfly
moving_objects.description: the only moving object: a blue (morpho-like) butterfly with black body/legs/antennae, flapping its wings while flying right-to-left across the frame
moving_objects.reference_point: body_x_fit, body_y_fit (thorax/body, robust quadratic fit of the detected black body) = best proxy for the rig origin; cx,cy (wing-mask centroid) and bbox_cx,bbox_cy also given

body_path_px.x_fit: x(f) = 2308.84 - 29.734 f - 0.01485 f^2  (f = frame), i.e. ~ -29.7 px/frame at start to ~ -31.8 px/frame at the end
body_path_px.note: measured body points scatter +-10-25 px about the fit because the body is partly hidden by the wings; mask centroid cx also advances ~-29 to -36 px/frame but oscillates with the wing beat
